- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for 30d horizon if sentiment >0.75.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) but true outcome spikes >10% above history, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to avoid overshoot.
- If supply_net is negative and bullish events outnumber bearish, model often over-anticipates price rise; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 18d mean if bullish events >20.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a spike, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 30d horizon if sentiment <0.25.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count (≥20) and net supply negative, model tends to overestimate peak; use 30d mean as baseline, then subtract 5–10% if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 → 0.00), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag in sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and supply_net is negative, model tends to under-forecast; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment ≤0.25 and supply_net < -10.00.
- For 30d forecasts with high volatility (e.g., 30d true outcome range >15%), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 10–20% downward correction if true outcome deviates >10% from 30d mean.
